stories.title: Startup Spotlight: Food photographer uses 25-year archive to build an AI tool that eliminates costly reshoots
stories.summary: Seattle photographer Scott Pitts uses his 25-year archive to train Pallat, an AI tool that lets art directors modify campaign photos in minutes. It eliminates costly reshoots while keeping studio craft central.
stories.extended_summary: Scott Pitts spent 25 years photographing food for major brands. Now, he's using that archive to train Pallat, an AI system that lets art directors tweak images—like adding tomatoes to a burger—without a reshoot. 'We're making sure those outputs look photoreal, that they're not going to get labeled as AI slop,' Pitts says. His non-technical background and photographic eye set Pallat apart from generic AI platforms. For a recent steakhouse shoot, Pallat saved the day, proving that domain expertise is key in generative tech.

stories.title: City Lens NYC featured at CUNY PIT pop-up
stories.summary: CUNY student Ashley Peguero built City Lens NYC, an AI-powered platform that makes complex city data accessible to everyday New Yorkers. From displacement risk to policy summaries, it's bridging the gap between data and community understanding.
stories.extended_summary: Ashley Peguero, a first-generation college student at CUNY, created City Lens NYC to help her Bronx community understand the data behind neighborhood changes. The platform combines over 50 public data sources with AI and interactive mapping, offering tools like a permit reader that flags displacement risk and a translator that turns dense policy text into plain language. Peguero's journey—from leaving high school at 17 to earning her GED at 24—fuels her mission to "bridge the gap between data and understanding and real life." Her work was recently showcased at a CUNY Public Interest Technology Lab pop-up at the Oculus.
